claims: Roughly three dozen countries, primarily in the Americas, offer unconditional birthright citizenship (jus soli).
Countries offering unconditional birthright citizenship automatically grant citizenship to almost anyone born within their territory, regardless of the parents' citizenship status.
United States offers unconditional birthright citizenship.
Costa Rica offers unconditional birthright citizenship.
Saint Lucia offers unconditional birthright citizenship.
Chile offers unconditional birthright citizenship with limitations.
Almost every country in the Western Hemisphere grants birthright citizenship.
Unconditional jus soli is rare outside the Americas.
Most of Europe and Asia operate under jus sanguinis.
Jus sanguinis is the right of blood.
Jus sanguinis is where citizenship is inherited from parents.
The UK abandoned universal birthright citizenship in 1983.
Australia abandoned universal birthright citizenship in 1986.
